title: Fix darwin OUTPUT_PATH_INVALID in the release supply chain (TMPDIR symlink realpath)
description:
Filed by architect-bdaffeaf 2026-08-20 from the first cross-host PUSH run's red evidence — the darwin defect blocking task-22cfca91's evidence pin.

EVIDENCE (push run 32351367576 at branch tip 0c32df9, job portability-evidence macos-latest, Integration gate leg, log quoted in msg-3cdc1e97): three named tests in tests/integration/release-supply-chain.test.mjs fail ONLY on darwin (ubuntu ran the same suite green): "cleans up on the signal path without replacing the outcome" (:781) — actual 'OUTPUT_PATH_INVALID' where expected undefined; "refuses conflicting durable content through the real publisher" (:818) false !== true; "publishes idempotently and refuses conflicting concurrent content" (:828) false !== true.

SUSPECT (measure, do not assume — stale-by-default): the macOS $TMPDIR symlink class — /var/folders/... is a symlink into /private/var, so a path guard comparing un-realpathed operands reads a legitimate temp destination as a path escape. The production suspect is the output-path validation in scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs (the OUTPUT_PATH_INVALID producer); the two false!==true failures are likely downstream of the same refusal poisoning the publisher fixtures. Reproduce the exact predicate: find where OUTPUT_PATH_INVALID is minted, determine which operand is un-realpathed, and fix by realpathing BOTH operands at the guard (never by weakening the guard or special-casing /private).

CONSUMERS: task-22cfca91 (portability shadow gate, BLOCKED — its evidence re-pin targets the commit carrying THIS fix; its worker's plan step 4 names darwin-red triage as in-scope routing) and the cross-host workflow itself. COORDINATION: scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs was touched by task-095cd7cc (DONE — rmSync options only); no in-flight owner at filing time. NOT in scope: workflow changes, evidence sealing, Windows/Linux behavior changes.
definitionOfDone: The exact darwin failure is reproduced and attributed: the OUTPUT_PATH_INVALID predicate's un-realpathed operand identified with file:line, recorded before any fix

The guard compares realpathed operands (or an equivalent symlink-safe containment check); the three named tests pass on darwin AND the guard still REFUSES a genuine escape — a test drives a real outside-the-root destination and asserts OUTPUT_PATH_INVALID survives (the fix must not weaken the fence)
All three previously-red tests pass in the cross-host PUSH run's macos portability-evidence job at the fix commit, and windows/ubuntu legs stay green — run id and count lines recorded

Mutation drill per epic rail 6: reverting the realpath (or the containment check) reds the named darwin-shaped test locally (simulate the symlinked-root shape with a junction/symlink fixture so the drill runs on any host)
pnpm test:integration green from PowerShell locally with count lines; production files <=250 lines; commit by explicit pathspec
taskRails: Fix the guard, never the test expectations: the three tests encode correct behavior; a fix that changes their assertions is a reject

Never special-case /private or darwin: realpath both operands (or prove an equivalent symlink-safe containment) so the same code is correct on every host — macOS $TMPDIR is one instance of a general symlinked-root class
The message format 'release temporary cleanup failed: ...' and the rmSync retry options landed by task-095cd7cc are frozen — do not disturb them
The external macos verification needs a PUSH run: request it via governor/human per the standing no-implicit-push rail; a Windows-local green is necessary but not sufficient for DoD 3

implementationPlan.description: ATTRIBUTION FIRST (DoD 1 — record before fixing). The mechanism, measured at filing and sharper than the filing's realpath guess — re-verify at your HEAD: publishEvidence (scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs:129-133) refuses OUTPUT_PATH_INVALID when `relative(root, target).startsWith("..")` OR `unsafeExistingPath(target)`; unsafeExistingPath (:117-127) walks the TARGET's ancestor chain ALL THE WAY to the filesystem root and returns true if ANY existing ancestor is a symbolic link. On macOS runners TMPDIR is /var/folders/... and /var ITSELF is a symlink to /private/var — so EVERY darwin temp-root target has a symlinked ancestor and every publish refuses. That explains all three reds from push run 32351367576 in one stroke: the signal-path test (:781) saw reason 'OUTPUT_PATH_INVALID' where undefined was expected; the two publisher tests (:818/:828) never got a first successful publish so their conflict/idempotence assertions read false. The guard's stated intent (comment :130-132) is to refuse a junction PLANTED BETWEEN evidenceRoot and the target — the walk just overshoots above the root the caller legitimately controls. Reproduce locally on Windows with the same shape: a directory junction/symlink ABOVE a legitimate evidenceRoot (mklink /J or fs.symlinkSync dir) must currently refuse — that repro is the drill fixture DoD 4 demands. Record the attribution (file:line, the overshoot, the repro output) in the step note. Baseline: `pnpm test:integration` from PowerShell, exit + counts verbatim (expect green on Windows — the defect is ancestor-shape-dependent).
implementationPlan.note:
ATTRIBUTION (DoD 1) recorded BEFORE any fix. Measured at HEAD 06c4e9e, win32, PowerShell.

PRODUCER, file:line. `git grep -n` gives exactly two OUTPUT_PATH_INVALID sites in scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs:
- :246 `if (!validInput(value))` — the INPUT layer (validInput :49 requires isAbsolute). This is the layer that answers the existing ":874 refuses traversal evidence roots" row (`evidenceRoot: "../escape"`), NOT the path guard. Recorded because epic rail 6 requires naming which layer refuses.
- :133 `if (relative(root, target).startsWith("..") || unsafeExistingPath(target))` — the PUBLISH layer, the darwin producer.

UN-BOUNDED OPERAND, file:line: `unsafeExistingPath` scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs:117-127. Loop 1 (:120, `while (!existsSync)`) climbs from the TARGET to its nearest existing ancestor; loop 2 (:121-124, `while (existsSync)`) then lstats every ancestor upward and `break`s only on `parent === cursor` — the FILESYSTEM ROOT. It takes no bound. Its JSDoc names the parameter `root` but :133 calls it with `target`; that name lie is plausibly how the missing bound survived review. On macOS $TMPDIR is /var/folders/... and /var is a symlink to /private/var, so loop 2 reaches /var and returns true for EVERY darwin temp-root target. The overshoot is above the evidenceRoot the caller legitimately controls — :130-132's own comment states the intent is a junction planted BETWEEN evidenceRoot and target.

PRE-FIX TRUTH TABLE, executed not argued. Probe in %TEMP% (deleted; never in the repo, never at the repo root — the suite's :930 leg spawns the real entry at REPO_ROOT), a VERBATIM copy of :117-127 driven over real `symlinkSync(..., "junction")` fixtures. `lstatSync(junction).isSymbolicLink()` is true on win32, which is why the darwin shape transfers to this host and no macOS lane is needed to see the red.

shape                                        want  shipped  bounded  atRoot  clause1
A ancestor-link above EXISTING root (darwin) false true     false    false   false
D ancestor-link above ABSENT root (prod)     false true     false    TRUE    false
B link IS nearest ancestor (test :878)       true  true     true     true    false
R evidenceRoot IS the link                   true  true     true     true    false
E link below root (test :886)                true  true     true     true    false

`bounded` = stop loop 2 at the nearest EXISTING ancestor of evidenceRoot, inclusive. `atRoot` = stop at the lexical evidenceRoot itself.

Four findings that change the plan's step-3 prescription (all measured):
1. `shipped` refuses A AND D. A is the darwin red. D is the PRODUCTION default shape (:310 evidenceRoot = join(repositoryRoot,"dist","release"); dist/ is gitignored so it is absent on a clean checkout) — so the overshoot is not darwin-only, it is one host-independent defect with two live shapes.
2. `bounded` equals `want` on all five rows. It is the only shape with no wrong cell.
3. `atRoot` — the plan's literal wording "walk up to (and including) the root itself" — is WRONG on D. When evidenceRoot does not exist, loop 1 has already climbed ABOVE it, so `cursor === root` can never fire and the bound degrades to the unbounded walk. This is why the ceiling must be root's nearest EXISTING ancestor (always reached, because loop 2 only ever visits existing paths). `atRoot` is therefore the drill-3 half-fix mutant, replacing the plan's "canonicalize target but not root" wording.
4. clause1 (`relative(root,target).startsWith("..")`) is FALSE on all five rows. The darwin refusal is 100% clause 2. root and target both derive lexically from the same `input.evidenceRoot` (target built at :295 by `join(String(input.evidenceRoot), sourceSha, evidenceDigest, "evidence.json")`), so the two operands are symmetric by construction and the containment compare is already symlink-safe. This is the "or prove an equivalent symlink-safe containment" branch of task rail 2, exercised end-to-end by the step-2(a) accept case. Realpathing is NOT required and is actively hazardous here: realpathing one operand alone moves the refusal from clause 2 to clause 1 with a byte-identical log, and realpathSync on evidenceRoot itself throws ENOENT on a clean checkout (D shape). No /private or darwin special-casing anywhere (rail 2).

BASELINE, fresh, PowerShell (the suite reds spuriously from Git Bash: :930 hits MSYS tar and refuses SOURCE_ARCHIVE_FAILED — a drill launched there starts from a 1-red baseline and misattributes):
`pnpm test:integration` -> EXIT=0; `Tests 360 passed (360)` (vitest leg) + `ℹ tests 66 / ℹ pass 66 / ℹ fail 0` (node:test leg, 4 suites). Green on Windows as predicted — the defect is ancestor-shape-dependent, and no fixture in the suite plants an A- or D-shape today, so nothing pins the bound. Count lines read, not just the exit code.

No files modified this step.

implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED. Three cases added to tests/integration/release-supply-chain.test.mjs inside the existing "release CLI and filesystem boundary" describe, immediately beside the guard's own arms (traversal :874, junction-is-nearest-ancestor :878, junction-below-root :886). CASES GENERATED — proven by the count, not claimed: node:test went 66 -> 69 tests. A sweep that silently produces zero cases is the epic's named failure mode; the +3 delta is the receipt.

(a) "publishes through a symlinked ancestor above an existing evidence root" — ACCEPT. Fixture: real dir R = temp(); junction L -> R; evidenceRoot = join(L, "root"), mkdirSync'd so the root EXISTS through the link. Every publish target therefore carries a symlinked ancestor ABOVE the root. This is the darwin $TMPDIR shape (/var -> /private/var) made host-independent: lstatSync(junction).isSymbolicLink() is true on win32 too, which is why no macOS lane is needed to see the red. Asserts ok:true, reason undefined, the evidence file exists on disk, and its parsed operation is "RECORDED" — bytes landing, not just a truthy verdict.

(b) "publishes through a symlinked ancestor above an absent evidence root" — ACCEPT. Fixture: junction L -> temp(); mkdirSync(L/repo); evidenceRoot = join(L, "repo", "dist", "release"), which does NOT exist. This is production's own shape (main() :310 passes join(repositoryRoot,"dist","release"); dist/ is gitignored) and it is the discriminator against the plan's literal "bound at the root itself" wording: when the root is absent, loop 1 has already climbed above it, so `cursor === root` never fires. Recorded here as a test rather than only as prose because that half-fix is otherwise invisible.

(c) "refuses an evidence root that is itself a junction to an outside destination" — REFUSE, the fence's other half (DoD 2). Fixture: outside = temp(); evidenceRoot IS a junction pointing at it. Asserts the exact reason code OUTPUT_PATH_INVALID via expectReleaseRefusal (which pins ok:false, code RELEASE_SUPPLY_CHAIN_REFUSED, reason, refusedBy) AND `readdirSync(outside)` deep-equals [] — a real outside-the-root destination that stays empty. This shape guards ceiling INCLUSIVITY — an exclusive ceiling accepts it and writes through the junction.

PLAN DEVIATION, stated: step-2(b) as written asks for a junction-below-root refuse case. That case already exists verbatim at :886 ("refuses a junction planted below the evidence root through the real publisher", junction at <root>/<sha>, plus its own readdirSync(outside) control) and every candidate bound holds it, so a duplicate would grade nothing. implementationPlan.description: GREEN — fix the guard in scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs, minimal and mechanism-true: anchor the symlink walk at the EVIDENCE ROOT boundary — canonicalize the root once (realpathSync on the deepest EXISTING ancestor of root, preserving the not-yet-created tail), recompute target relative to the canonical root, and walk ONLY the span from target up to (and including) the root itself — never above it. A symlink at-or-below root still refuses (case b); a symlinked ancestor ABOVE root (darwin /var) no longer does (case a); relative-containment check now compares canonicalized operands so the same fix closes the /var vs /private/var relative() mismatch. Keep the function's try/catch fail-closed shape (any fs error → unsafe). The frozen surfaces stay frozen: the cleanup message format and rmSync retry options (task-095cd7cc) untouched; the file stays <=250 lines-ish per its current size (measure; it is production — split is available but unlikely needed for ~10 changed lines). implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs only; no test assertion touched (task rail 1).

THE FIX. `unsafeExistingPath` (:117 pre-fix) took one argument and ran two loops: loop 1 climbed from the target to its nearest existing ancestor, loop 2 then lstat'd upward and broke only on `parent === cursor`, the filesystem root. Now:
- new `nearestExistingPath(path)` — loop 1, extracted so both ends use the same ascent.
- `unsafeExistingPath(target, evidenceRoot)` — loop 2 climbs from `nearestExistingPath(target)` and stops on `cursor === ceiling` where `ceiling = nearestExistingPath(evidenceRoot)`. The break sits AFTER the lstat, so the ceiling is INCLUSIVE: a junction standing at the evidence root itself still refuses.
- call site :133 -> :137 now passes `root` as the bound: `unsafeExistingPath(target, root)`.
- the :130-132 comment claimed the walk "covers every existing ancestor up to the filesystem root". That is now false, so it was rewritten to state the real contract.

WHY THE CEILING IS THE ROOT'S NEAREST EXISTING ANCESTOR, NOT THE ROOT. Deviation from the plan's literal step-3 wording ("up to and including the root itself"), forced by the step-1 measurement: when the evidence root does not exist, loop 1 has ALREADY climbed above it, so `cursor === root` can never fire and the bound silently degrades to the unbounded walk with a byte-identical log. That absent-root case is production's default (:314 passes join(repositoryRoot,"dist","release"); dist/ is gitignored). The probe scored it `atRoot` and it is wrong on the D row. `nearestExistingPath(evidenceRoot)` is always an existing path and loop 2 only ever visits existing paths, so the bound is always reached. The step-2(b) test exists precisely to pin this, and drill 3 in step 4 will red it.

WHY NO realpathSync. Deviation from the plan's "canonicalize the root once / recompute target relative to the canonical root", taken under task rail 2's explicit alternative ("or prove an equivalent symlink-safe containment"), on three measured grounds:
1. The containment clause was FALSE on all five probed shapes — the darwin refusal is 100% clause 2, so canonicalizing clause 1 fixes nothing measurable.
2. `root` and `target` are symmetric by construction: target is built at :299 as `join(String(input.evidenceRoot), sourceSha, evidenceDigest, "evidence.json")` from the same string, and both are `resolve()`d together at :133. Lexical-vs-lexical is already symlink-safe. Canonicalizing ONE end is the known trap — it moves the refusal from clause 2 to clause 1 with an identical log.
3. Canonicalizing the other end is worse than useless here: realpathSync RESOLVES a planted junction, which is exactly the redirect this guard exists to refuse (the planningNotes reject that as approach (a)), and realpathSync on an absent evidenceRoot throws ENOENT on a clean checkout. The shipped fix never calls realpathSync — it only string-climbs and lstats — so it is ENOENT-immune by construction.
No /private, no darwin, no platform branch anywhere: one code path, correct on every host (rail 2).

NOT WEAKENED. lstat semantics are byte-identical inside the bounded span — a symlink is still a symlink even when it resolves back inside the root, so the planted-junction defence is unchanged. The fail-closed try/catch is intact and now also covers both ascents (any fs error -> `return true` -> refuse). Frozen surfaces untouched (task rail 3): `release temporary cleanup failed: ...` and cleanRoots' rmSync retry options are in a different function and show no diff.

VERIFICATION, fresh, PowerShell:
- `node --test tests/integration/release-supply-chain.test.mjs` -> EXIT=0; `ℹ tests 69 / ℹ pass 69 / ℹ fail 0`. Both step-2 accept cases flipped RED->GREEN; the new refuse case, the traversal row, the junction-is-nearest-ancestor row (:878), the junction-below-root row (:886), the hostile symlink-output row and all 66 pre-existing cases stayed green.
- `pnpm typecheck:release` -> EXIT=0. This is the leg that actually covers this file (--allowJs --checkJs over scripts/release/*.mjs); `typecheck:packaging`, which `test:integration` chains, only covers tools/packaging/*.ts and would NOT have caught the JSDoc arity change. Execution witnessed by the `$ tsc --noEmit --strict --allowJs --checkJs ... scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs` echo, not by the exit code alone.

SIZE, disclosed not hidden: scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs is 319 lines, up from 314 at HEAD (+5). It was already above the epic's 250-line target before this task and remains well below the 400-line split line. Splitting it is not attempted here: the suite asserts whole-file regexes over this source and spawns the real entry, so a split is a separate task with its own drills, and this change is +5 lines on an unrelated axis.

implementationPlan.note:
MUTATION DRILLS (DoD 4) + adversarial review.

DRILL METHOD. Restore is a byte copy from %TEMP%\sc-backup-942bf3fc.mjs, NEVER `git checkout` — the fix is uncommitted at drill time, so a git restore would have destroyed it. Each drill asserts the needle was FOUND and that the file hash CHANGED before running, so a drill that applied nothing cannot read as green. After each: `Copy-Item` back and SHA-256 compared to the pre-drill hash 25CF394D4A5A60ABF4266F5A91AD5DFF8593335BEF50070662943AD7463319EB. All four printed "restored ok"; final "FINAL HASH MATCH: True". Run from PowerShell (the suite reds spuriously from Git Bash on the MSYS tar leg). Post-drill `git diff --numstat` is exactly `12 7 scripts/release/supply-chain.mjs` and `45 0 tests/...` — no drill residue.

D1 — REVERT THE ROOT-ANCHORING (delete `if (cursor === ceiling) break;`, walk to the filesystem root again). tests 69 / pass 67 / fail 2:
  ✖ publishes through a symlinked ancestor above an existing evidence root
  ✖ publishes through a symlinked ancestor above an absent evidence root
The darwin shape, killed on this host. Note the FIRST attempt at this drill printed "NEEDLE NOT FOUND - DRILL INVALID" because the needle carried CRLF and the file is LF; it was re-run with the correct needle rather than counted as a pass. A silent no-op here would have looked identical to a surviving mutant.

D2 — DROP THE FENCE (`if (lstatSync(cursor).isSymbolicLink())` -> `if (false)`). tests 69 / pass 66 / fail 3:
  ✖ refuses a junction planted below the evidence root through the real publisher
  ✖ refuses a not-yet-created evidence root beneath a junction
  ✖ refuses an evidence root that is itself a junction to an outside destination
Exactly the three fence arms and nothing else. The fix does not weaken the guard: remove the lstat and all three refusals vanish.

D3 — THE HALF-FIX (`nearestExistingPath(evidenceRoot)` -> `resolve(evidenceRoot)`, i.e. bound at the lexical root). tests 69 / pass 68 / fail 1:
  ✖ publishes through a symlinked ancestor above an absent evidence root
Substituted for the plan's "canonicalize target but not root" wording, which does not apply because the shipped fix uses no realpath. This is the equivalent proof that the OTHER half matters: it isolates the exact half-fix a reviewer would propose, and only the absent-root case can see it. Without the step-2(b) test this mutant survives silently and production's own clean-checkout shape stays broken.

D4 — FAIL-CLOSED POSITIVE CONTROL (`throw` injected at the top of the walk's try). tests 69 / pass 56 / fail 13. Every success path red; the three fence arms and the traversal row stayed GREEN. The catch arm is reached, returns true, and REFUSES — it does not crash and does not accept. This replaces the plan's "make realpathSync throw via a dangling link" drill, which is inapplicable since the fix calls no realpathSync. It also witnesses that the guard is on every success path, including ":930 records truthful evidence through the actual package script" (18.5s, the real production entry).

POST-DRILL GREEN, fresh: `node --test tests/integration/release-supply-chain.test.mjs` -> EXIT=0, tests 69 / pass 69 / fail 0, with all three previously-darwin-red tests named green: ✔ cleans up on the signal path without replacing the outcome; ✔ refuses conflicting durable content through the real publisher; ✔ publishes idempotently and refuses conflicting concurrent content. Every fence arm green too: ✔ refuses traversal evidence roots before external work; ✔ refuses a not-yet-created evidence root beneath a junction; ✔ refuses a junction planted below the evidence root through the real publisher; ✔ refuses an evidence root that is itself a junction to an outside destination.

ADVERSARIAL CHECKLIST.
- Temp-rename path: UNAFFECTED. No canonicalization was introduced, so `targetDir` and `${targetDir}.tmp-${pid}-${uuid}` still derive from `resolve(request.evidencePath)` byte-for-byte as before; the diff has zero lines below the guard. No cross-device rename risk was created.
- TOCTOU: not widened. The existsSync/lstat ordering inside the walk is unchanged; the only new reads are the ceiling ascent, taken once BEFORE the walk. If the tree mutates mid-walk the cursor simply misses the ceiling and the walk runs to the filesystem root — the old behaviour, i.e. refuse. Fail-closed in every direction. The separate guard-to-write window is a pre-existing defect and is untouched.
- Ceiling unreachable: if evidenceRoot is not an ancestor of target, `cursor === ceiling` never fires and the walk degrades to the pre-fix unbounded form. That is strictly the stricter direction, not an escape, and clause 1 already refuses same-drive non-contained targets first.
- Windows drive-letter casing: `d:\x` vs `D:\x` would make the equality miss and the walk over-refuse. Fail-closed, and unreachable in practice — both operands derive from the same `input.evidenceRoot` string at :299.
- Windows junctions: covered by the same lstat, p
